title: Candidate Search Loop Invariant
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, and $q$ a rational number. For every natural number $dd$ and register state $\sigma$, suppose the vertex count minus the candidate counter, with truncated natural subtraction, equals $dd$; every register is at most $B$; the candidate counter $u$ is at most the vertex count $n$; the current-vertex register is zero; and the saved pointer $q_0$ plus $2n+2$ is at most $B$. For every $j\ge u$ with $j<n$, if the binary expansion of $j$ is doubled at position $q_0$ in $x$, then the configuration at the specified state with candidate and current-vertex registers set to $j$, pointer set to $q_0+2|\mathrm{bits}(j)|+2$, and scratch register cleared has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If there is no $j$ with $u\le j<n$ whose binary expansion is doubled at position $q_0$ in $x$, then $q=0$. The configuration at the search-loop state with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
